title: Fenwick d'Jorasco
dek: Founder of Vital Chain, healer and investigator of Eovar: Fenwick turns knowledge into public work, healing networks and magical routes, while his hunger for understanding carries its own dangers.

facts.Affiliations: Vital Chain · Ale-Chemy Knights · The Seekers · Veilguard

body:
Fenwick d'Jorasco turns discoveries into things other people can use. In Eovar Harbor, that work includes healing, renewal, public bounties and information gathered from ordinary residents. In Gael, it becomes travel planning and proposals for a permanent base. His curiosity also brings him into dangerous magic: the same desire to understand that builds institutions can tempt him to possess power.

Reading Eovar’s heartbeat

Fenwick spends a day walking Eovar’s streets, speaking with familiar locals and helping at the infirmary through mundane medicine. He listens to patients and workers, tracks ships and traffic, notices closures, speaks with Robben and asks the Blind Beggar what he has observed from the harbor.

Back at his tower with tea, he tries to connect those small irregularities. His intelligence depends on participation in the city. The people who heal, work, watch and gossip become part of how he understands the port.

Harbor Master Raven Joyner later credits Fenwick and the Ale-Chemy Knights with good work that improves lives, while also remembering adventurer disruption. Civic usefulness and a complicated reputation coexist.

Vital Chain and a city’s renewal

Ada’s account of 27 January 2025 identifies Fenwick as a halfling wizard, healer, civic rebuilder and founder of Vital Chain. It connects him directly with Eovar’s renewal. The date records recognition of an existing institution, rather than fixing its founding day.

Through Vital Chain, other people can seek healing, community, connectedness and spiritual restoration. The network takes its place among the emerging adventurer organizations and extends the care Fenwick can offer beyond his own spellcasting.

The guild that proved difficult to build

Fenwick attempts to organize a broader adventurers’ guild. Independent, powerful people dispersed across islands prove difficult to centralize; the effort is remembered as failed or partial rather than as an established unified guild.

Tobias Goodbarrel suspects Fenwick may abandon that model and pursue similar goals through the Ale-Chemy Knights. This is Tobias’s interpretation of Fenwick’s direction. It does not establish Fenwick’s private plan or make Vital Chain, the guild attempt and the Knights the same organization.

A tower with work for other people

By February 2025, Tobias directs newcomers to Fenwick’s Tower and its notice board for open material bounties. Residence and public work meet in one place: adventurers can find a job without waiting for a formal expedition.

Tobias also recommends Fenwick for deeper knowledge of Eovar and contacts concerning the Thieves Guild. His directions give newcomers someone to ask when a map or a notice board cannot answer their questions.

The Silver Spire · becoming a citizen

His Wizarding Clock Tower grows into the Silver Spire Public Baths, Arcane Market & Healing House. Fenwick chooses Eovar after witnessing neglect and helping its infirmary. Free private bathing, food, shelter and medical overflow turn his resources toward ordinary neighbors; an arcane market later joins the building’s public services.

Tobias helps build the tower and is trusted to house-sit. Its four floors ascend from public care to staff and raven communications, flexible secure rooms and Fenwick’s private magical workspace. He proposes an island-wide raven network and later casts Simulacrum upstairs. His suggestion of petrifying prisoners for storage remains a proposal, exposing the unsettling extremes his practical reasoning can reach.

One cold, foggy evening, he fills the first floor with families, food and a gentler illusionary battle for children. At the baths’ celebration he speaks of loving Eovar’s people; the later public notice is signed as a citizen. “We are Eovar” gives words to a belonging expressed through work.

The Spire becomes part of a broader vision of sewers, food security, docks, healing and a city able to support itself. The vision extends beyond the work established as complete.

October 2024 · grievance and instigation

After unrest around Melian and the burning of her house, Olokun asks whether a woman might have caused the fire. Fenwick wonders whether she is manufacturing the mood or adding fuel to genuine anger.

He distinguishes a grievance from the people who might exploit it. His suspicion does not identify the arsonist or prove that the crowd is controlled. In the same broad period, he steps before a crowd despite visible shyness and nerves: usefulness and persistence support an authority that is not effortless charisma.

The Spiral · knowledge and contamination

The Spiral is both beautiful and harmful to Fenwick. He describes gaining Deep Speech while his body is cursed, asks whether he will always remain changed, and tries to understand altered inscriptions and everything the walls can offer.

His declaration that magic can let him have it both ways expresses a real temptation. Useful understanding and bodily harm arrive together; fascination with the Spiral’s power cannot be reduced to harmless scholarship.

Later his limbs straighten, movement returns and somatic casting becomes possible again. Recovery does not erase the experience. The exact sequence and dates of the Spiral’s effects remain incomplete.

Ingenuity, limits and “the returned”

When a map is magically obscured, Fenwick tries indirect views through reflections, eyes, glasses and tools. The attempt shows how readily he questions what a restriction actually prevents. Ingenuity can reveal options, while also making boundaries difficult for him to accept.

Later appearances call him “the returned” and “of Eovar.” The title is preserved, but the current account does not settle a death, a return date or a mechanism. Those details should remain open.

Making Gael reachable

At the Tower of Gael, Fenwick explains how Teleportation Circle can reach the area and Word of Recall can return the group. He accounts for high-level spell resources already spent and frames the mission as scouting because the party lacks enough information.

He later proposes an Ale-Chemy hunting lodge in Gael, joining access to the Plains with hunting, research into Nuru and Death, library work and ruin exploration. The proposal establishes an intended base, not proof that the lodge was completed.

Papirak · concern, suspicion and trust

During the investigation of Papirak’s death, Fenwick challenges the suggestion that an isolated elderly wizard may have died through mundane accident and asks about the missing spellbook. Camilla reads his interest in valuable knowledge as potentially opportunistic. Her suspicion remains her perspective; it is not an established theft.

At the funeral on 30 September 2026, Pell permits Fenwick to cast Sequester on the Staff of Power before it is buried with Papirak. Its disappearance from magical detection alarms Camilla. Melian trusts Pell and Fenwick and continues the burial.

The mausoleum and funeral record preserve the public act of stewardship. Security over the staff does not give Fenwick ownership of it.

A bridge to the Knights’ network

Fenwick’s early connection to Farkur’s planning grows into public promotion of Ryvyting Creations and its advertised spell collection. This makes him a significant civic and magical ally of the Ale-Chemy Knights, without establishing him as a founder or merging his own institutions with theirs.

The Silver Spire concentrates his personal resources into local care and public space; the Knights distribute work through scouts, crafters, builders and transport. Their overlapping goals do not establish Knights ownership of the Spire.

The work that can outlast him

Vital Chain, the tower’s notice board, Eovar’s information networks, guild experiments and Gael travel plans give other people ways to seek care, work, information and passage. Fenwick repeatedly tries to make what he knows usable beyond his own journeys.

His strengths and risks grow together. Curiosity, healing and logistical magic expand other people’s options; a hunger for knowledge can become possession, and a network centered on one person can become dependent on that person. His civic work matters without resolving those tensions.

October · recording the forest’s questions

Fenwick travels with Ryvyt, Saelihn and Trougar from Emberwillow Bridge to ruins near Larkhollow. He samples river water, records directions and studies the site. True Seeing reveals the marking that activates the small figure in Viota’s monument. He calls for restraint when the watching child has not attacked and brings a rubbing back for translation.

His civic work in Eovar continues to matter, while these scenes show him acting as a mobile investigator. The separate Legend Lore response is not included in the continuation, so its contents are not added to his public findings.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

Aid before trade

During the pirate hostage crisis, Fenwick, Brianna and Ithilrune visit a rebuilding coastal refugee settlement on Gael. Edgar, who is organizing fishing and construction, reports eight captives and three pirate ships; those numbers are his account. Fenwick unloads the Knights’ gifts and helps move residents toward the tower for safety. Brianna entertains the children with conjured snow. Edgar asks for building materials, furniture, cooking equipment, healing kits and livestock, and welcomes a proposed Knights outpost. The settlement has about two hundred people by his estimate and no chosen name. The branch establishes delivered aid and a prospective relationship, not a completed outpost, a hostage rescue or an identification with later refugee groups.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

An investment conversation

Fenwick asks Paetr the Counter about future investment in Eovar. Paetr offers examples of returns depending on the amount and term. These are a banker’s advertised terms, not verified earnings: the exchange records no deposit or completed investment.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3.

March 2025 · writing for the next traveler

Fenwick’s first-exploration guide to Gael combines arrival advice, research, loneliness and warnings. His location notes preserve his account of solitary study in Nuru’s library, his caution on the coastal stairs, his withdrawal from the cathedral and a dangerous Plains expedition.

His player frames the guide as work to bring back to Pristinia and invites correction. Its value includes the limits of a first visit: speculation about the Tower’s light, interpretations of ruined statues and collected stories about Hope remain his contemporary understanding. Neither the guide’s later usefulness nor his growing expertise makes those early theories automatically true.

Library work with other people

In the Library of Nuru, Fenwick’s simulacrum brings food to Scribonia, while Fenwick offers access to his spells and begins copying from Scribonia’s collection. Minerva joins the discussion of Mage’s Ruin. Scribonia plans to open its lead layer after gathering a group; Fenwick offers support without claiming that the work is already done.

Fenwick leaves a draft field guide to Verdelune in the library and later checks on Minerva by Sending. She says she is safe and has gained entry to Nerithra. The exchange gives him a report, without revealing the ritual’s outcome or every detail of her whereabouts.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

The new Tower record finds Fenwick returning to Gael, then later teleporting to the Tower and secluding himself to rest. Those appearances extend his travel history without establishing that the proposed Mage’s Ruin expedition has occurred or succeeded.

The rescue and its destructive cost

Fenwick follows Lirael’s direction in the search for Selwyn. During the river passage, Pin ages seven years despite Ryvyt’s intervention. Beyond it, Fenwick fights the figures around a rooted body and prepares a way to get the company out.

The search also damages the forest. Fire brings a sense of anguish from a tree, and Fenwick’s later meteor spell starts a forest fire. Minerva’s negotiation finally obtains the body’s release in exchange for remaining with the figures. At this stage, preparing a teleport does not show a completed departure, and release from the roots does not establish Selwyn’s later condition.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.

Joining without surrendering another obligation

On 23 October 2026, Severina asks whether he would join the Veilguard. Fenwick wants his knowledge to help Gael and asks whether he can retain his Ale-Chemy Knights affiliation. She explicitly says he can and formally welcomes him.

He accepts, repeats the words and promises she can count on him. The scene establishes a new obligation alongside the older one, not the merger of two factions. The requested relics and later campaigns remain plans.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Preserving the body does not remove the branch

After the search for Selwyn, Fenwick considers the black branch still lodged in the body. He later casts Gentle Repose. The narrator confirms the spell’s effects while expressly leaving the branch unchanged. This is a limited, witnessed result rather than a restoration of Selwyn to life.

Guides, roads and another kind of preparation

Fenwick produces a draft guide to Verdelune after working through his notes in the Library of Nuru. The accompanying story note describes his intention to revise it and the Gael guide; it does not make every conclusion in an unreviewed attachment established fact.

At Crustacean Cove he gathers shells with fertilizer in mind, studies an illusory map and discusses roads with Kar’nak. He wants to connect important sites, especially the Mage’s Ruin and the teleportation circle, and says a town should come first. No road or town is completed in this conversation. Later he joins Severina and Ryvyt on a hunt, seeking advice on using his spells more effectively beside them.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2025-01-15 · compatible RP

    Vital Chain in proposal form

    Fenwick shares a draft for coordinated medical care, public health and readiness in Eovar and Pristinia. He still speaks conditionally about opening branches.

    Known at this stage
    The named institution and its intended scope exist in his proposal.
    Consequence
    This supplies an earlier stage before Ada’s later public recognition.
    Still unresolved
    It does not date a legal founding or establish two completed branches.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

  2. 2025-01-13 · compatible RP

    An edited public notice

    A tower notice advertises the Silver Spire’s baths, market and healing house. It explicitly records a later July edit.

    Known at this stage
    The surviving text is an edited notice, not a securely January-dated opening announcement.
    Consequence
    Public service is documented while the opening chronology remains bounded.
    Still unresolved
    The original posting timestamp cannot date every sentence of the edited text.

    Receipt 1

  3. 2025-03-11 → 2025-03-13 · player testimony

    Writing for later travelers

    Fenwick frames his location guide as correctable notes and records a dangerous Plains visit.

    Known at this stage
    He writes from visits, research and reports with different degrees of certainty.
    Consequence
    His practical knowledge can help others without becoming objective regional history.
    Still unresolved
    The casualty account is not automatically identical to every earlier Sildithas death.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

profile.personality: Curious, persistent and useful before he is charismatic. His instinct to understand a problem produces shared systems, but dangerous knowledge can tempt him toward possession.
profile.achievements: Founded Vital Chain, built the Silver Spire’s public baths and healing services in Eovar, provided a public bounty board and planned magical travel in Gael. Secured Papirak’s Staff of Power with Sequester during the funeral. Delivered Knights aid to the Gael refugee settlement during the hostage crisis and helped move residents toward safety; an outpost remained a proposal. Supports the Selwyn expedition and spell exchange, then accepts the Veilguard’s mutual obligations.
profile.relationships: Tobias directs newcomers toward his knowledge and public work. Melian can disagree with him while trusting his funeral work; Camilla’s suspicions remain attributed. Vessalia, Di’Trillio, Pell and Minerva are his fellow Seekers.
